sections.heading: What this dossier is
sections.body: AL052026 — Tropical Depression Five, declared as Invest 97L — is live in the north-central Gulf. Storm Atlas neither forecasts it nor states a landfall: the archive holds twelve storms formed within 250 km of the declared cell, August–September, from 1971.

sections.heading: Why 28.0°N 88.7°W and not the live centre
sections.body: The query runs at a declared pre-genesis reference cell, 28.0°N 88.7°W, not at the live centre, 28.2°N 91.5°W. NHC has since opened advisories, but an advisory package is not the archive’s genesis definition: AL052026 is absent from the pack, and the operational layer is not a cohort source. The cell was not revised to the centre.

sections.heading: Reading the outcome panel
sections.body: Scoreable rows are exact n/N with a 95% Wilson interval; read the interval, not the point. CONUS is two questions — any intensity 10 of 12 (83.3%, 55-95%), hurricane force 1 of 12 (8.3%, 1-35%). Two rows are stamped unscoreable, their intervals void.

sections.heading: Radius, month window and season floor
sections.body: Three frames on the hurricane-force trigger row: 1 of 12 at 250 km Aug–Sep; 0 of 5 at 150 km, refused; 2 of 17 over all months.

sections.heading: Historical transit times
sections.body: Timing quantiles sit outside the minimum-sample rule, unstamped at any n; only TS clears the 10-case threshold. n=22 counts landfall rows, not storms: FERN 1971 supplies 12 of the 22, so over half that spread is one track re-counted.

sections.heading: The analog plate
sections.body: Eight of twelve print under the archive’s rule: majors first, then hurricanes, peak descending. A selection, not a ranking. Tracks are history, not a cone.

sections.heading: COMMERCIAL READ — interpretation, not a rate
sections.body:
• Insured-region adjacency. These rows are CONUS-wide, not Gulf-coast: the archive scores no sub-CONUS region, and crossings include Florida as well as Texas and Louisiana. 10 of 12 crossed at any intensity (83.3%, 55-95%); 1 of 12 at ≥64 kt (8.3%, 1-35%). A hurricane-force attachment rests on one archived event. Bound or challenge a rate set elsewhere; do not derive one.
  • Energy adjacency and timing. Transit to a CONUS crossing is a median 65.5 h, its upper quartile largely one 1971 track re-counted.
  • BASIS RISK. ANITA 1977 formed 126 km from this cell and struck Tamaulipas; ALICIA 1983 formed 194 km from it and struck Texas — one cell, two coasts. Peak is not landfall intensity: FERN 1971 peaked at 80 kt, its Louisiana crossings 25 kt.

sections.heading: What is not here
sections.body:
Refused by the instrument. No Hawaii rate: hawaii:any OUT OF SCOPE for a North Atlantic cohort; hawaii:hurricane BASE RATE ONLY, 2 events archive-wide against 10. No rates at all at 150 km, where N=5.

No genesis point. The archive returns none for AL052026: no cohort here is keyed to this storm’s formation.

Out of scope. No state-level landfall row, and no unconditional number — that would need an external formation probability on the same formation event and conditioning set.

answers.adds: The alternative is not a public map but your own IBTrACS or HURDAT2 query, which a cat modelling team can write. Storm Atlas adds the declared cohort, exact n/N with 95% Wilson intervals, printed refusals, a replay URL.
answers.commercial: It gives a basis-risk file one component that can be tested: a cohort a counterparty reopens from a URL and reproduces line for line, misses included.

sections.body: Storm Atlas is a research-only historical engine answering one fixed question: from this declared genesis condition, in this season window, what did the record go on to do? N = 12, ESS 12, SUFFICIENT against a minimum sample of 10.

sections.heading: Why a replayable cohort is trigger documentation
sections.body: A parametric trigger’s basis-risk file needs a prior a counterparty can reopen, not a number in a deck. The cohort is a URL: cell, radius, month window, season floor and methodology version travel in it, so the same query returns the same n/N and interval on any desk, and the denominator is named.

sections.heading: Near-misses: where the basis risk is
sections.body: NEAR MISSES. Anita 1977 formed 126 km from the cell and struck Tamaulipas at 120 kt — inside the cohort, outside the CONUS row. Alicia 1983 formed 194 km out and struck Texas at 100 kt: the single member behind CONUS — ≥64 kt, and at 150 km not a member. Barry 2019 formed 110 km out with a 65 kt Louisiana landfall, but its 11 July genesis is outside the window.

sections.heading: Basis risk — read before writing the trigger
sections.body:
• Same genesis cell ≠ same landfall. Twelve storms formed inside one 250 km circle and went to Texas, Louisiana, Florida and Tamaulipas.
  • Same class ≠ same local outcome. The archive scores a crossing and its intensity, not a footprint or a loss.
  • A CONUS row is not a state row. No state-level landfall is scored, at any radius or sample size.
  • The interval is the precision. 1 of 12 is 8.3%, 95% Wilson 1-35%.

sections.heading: Where this sits in the workflow
sections.body: Cohort research, trigger design and counterparty explanation — not live pricing.

sections.heading: Geography is not a probability
sections.body: Landfall resolves to region, not state: CONUS, Mexico, Caribbean, Central America, Hawaii and unattributed, each an “any” and a “>=64 kt” form. Both Hawaii rows are refused here — OUT OF SCOPE and BASE RATE ONLY. There is no Texas, Louisiana or Gulf-state row to quote. The paths on the plate are geometry, not a rate.

sections.heading: Commercial reading — what the rows cover
sections.body: Two hurricane landfalls, opposite sides of the basin. CONUS — >=64 kt is 1 of 12 (8.3%, 1-35%); MEXICO — >=64 kt is 1 of 12 (8.3%, 1-35%). ANITA 1977 is the Mexican one, Tamaulipas at 120 kt; ALICIA 1983 the CONUS one, Texas at 100 kt. The rates are region rows — a CONUS row, not a Texas one.

sections.heading: Read the band, not the point
sections.body: The interval, not the point estimate, is the research input. The same cell at 150 km returns N=5 against min sample 10 — BELOW MIN SAMPLE, every row RATE REFUSED.

sections.heading: What this is not
sections.body: No prices, no trades, no view on gas, power, refined products or freight. No state rates. Every row is genesis-conditioned and assumes formation: no unconditional number is computed here, and no NHC outlook probability is multiplied by these rows — the composition rule is in the footer. Landfall is counted jointly, never decomposed.

sections.heading: Where Karina sits against her genesis cohort
sections.body: The archive supports exactly two rarity statements here: 1 of 14 reached Cat 4, 0 of 14 reached Cat 5, each with its interval. A percentile or a rank against the basin or the season needs a denominator this cohort does not define, so Storm Atlas does not compute one. The refusal is the result.

sections.heading: Land rows, printed as the engine returned them
sections.body: Every land row is published, zeros and stamps included: Mexico — any 1 of 14 (7.1%, 1-31%), ≥64 kt 0 of 14 (0.0%, 0-22%). The rest return OUT OF SCOPE or BASE RATE ONLY.

sections.heading: Commercial reading — labelled interpretation
sections.body: Rarity and pathway context for research or a client conversation — not threat monitoring. The cohort says how often storms that began here climbed this far, and nothing about where Karina goes.

answers.adds: The outlook gives a chance of forming; the cone gives a track if it does. Neither says that twelve North Atlantic storms formed within 250 km of the declared 97L cell in August or September since 1971, that ten reached TS, or which twelve they were.
answers.commercial: Worked here: the 97L cohort returns CONUS ≥64 kt at 1 of 12 — 8.3%, 95% Wilson 1-35% — on a denominator a counterparty can open and read storm by storm. The interval, not the point, is what a candidate trigger must survive. No price call, no recommendation, no skill claim.

sections.body: A research-only historical genesis/outcome engine for the North Atlantic and East Pacific: give it a genesis point or a declared pre-genesis reference cell and it returns what the record did next as exact n/N with a 95% Wilson interval, names every storm in the denominator, and refuses what the record cannot carry.

• Condition on a point. A genesis position or a declared pre-genesis reference cell, with a stated radius and month window. Rates assume formation — not P(forms), not a live feed, not a cone.
  • Retrieve the analog tracks. Every storm in the cohort, and representative members under a stated rule with genesis date, distance from the cell, peak and their own landfalls. Nothing is ranked a closest analog.
  • Compare contract rows. Reached TD, TS and Cat 1–5, each exact n/N with a 95% Wilson interval; six landfall regions, each an “any” and a ≥64 kt pair. State-level landfall is not scored.
  • Read the refusals as output. Below min sample: counts, no rate, no interval. Move the cell and watch N and the refusal move with it.

An interpolated fix never establishes a threshold crossing, so time-to-hurricane is never dated off a wind nobody measured. A cohort’s defining variable is not reported back as an outcome of it, with one exception left in the open: every cohort returns reached TD at 100%, because a cohort is storms that formed. Below min sample a rate is refused rather than estimated. An absent outcome is not a zero. Every figure carries a pack stamp and a URL that reproduces it.

A browser and replayable cohort URLs. A URL carries the cell, radius, season floor, month window, basin and methodology version, so a reviewer opens the same cohort and reads the same counts, rates, intervals and refusals.
PROPOSED / PILOT — not available today. Exportable charts. An API. Recurring institutional briefs. None of the three exists yet.

Three cohorts, as the engine returned them. The cell is an input, not an observation, and the URL records the choice. Karina is read at a declared point: the archive holds no genesis row for EP112026.
